stories.summary: The Ukrainian president says wartime elections, as called for by the ex-defense minister, could "split Ukraine." He also said Russia was planning to mobilize hundreds of thousands of troops after September polls there.

"I believe that in a war like this, elections as such are a huge risk. Elections right now are a tsunami for the country that will split Ukraine," Zelenskyy said in remarks released on Sunday. Under martial law, elections are currently suspended in the country as it fights the invading Russian forces. The measure has wide public support. What did Zelenskyy say about the proposed election? "If we want to destroy the country, then we can move in the direction of elections during these times of war," Zelenskyy said in the firm rejection of the proposal by former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov. An unknown number of homes have been destroyed and at least six people have been injured. Officials have expanded the "GO NOW" zone to include almost 90,000 residents as conditions make the fire unpredicatable. What do we know about the Hawk Fire in Nevada? About 42,000 residents were ordered to evacuate, with another 45,000 told to be ready to leave, officials said. stories.summary: Prosecutors and police in Munich believe they have identified the man who set a 1970 fire at a Jewish community center and old people's home that killed seven people. But he died in 2020, so prosecution is not possible.
stories.article_text_excerpt: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5J7uF The 1970 arson attack on a Jewish religious center in central Munich killed seven people [FILE: February 13, 1970] Image: Joachim Barfknecht/dpa/picture alliance Advertisement Munich 's Public Prosecutor's Office believes it has solved one of the worst antisemitic attacks in post-war German history. Police and prosecutors said on Thursday that new investigations point "clearly" towards the involvement of a man who died in 2020. Additional information came to light after his death which led to the case being reopened in April 2025. Now, with investigators satisfied that the culprit is identified — but with no scope to prosecute the deceased and no known indications of accomplices — they are closing the file once again. stories.title: Minors living alone on Ceuta's streets at risk of abuse
stories.summary: Several thousand unaccompanied minors have gathered in Ceuta, a Spanish enclave on the northern coast of Africa. Illness and abuse are rife, and the authorities admit they are overwhelmed.
